main_text.l: sub illis continentur, accuratius applicavisse, ejus mentem & sensum clarius aperuisse, Christianorum officia tanquam rivulos ex hoc fonte deduxisse, & consequentias ex hoc principio derivandas; distinxisse quæ jure licita sunt, & ex mente Legis ab iis quæ pro tempore sunt tolerata, non approbata, propter cordis hominum duritiem; res ad principium revocasse, & eas restituisse prout erant in principio; exemplum sanctitatis longè perfectissimum nobis dedisse imitandum; interdixisse ea quæ Lex prohibebat quidem, at tolerabat ratione πολιτείας ad tempus, ingenium, & mores Judæorum accommodatæ; vim & robur præceptis Legis, & nostræ ad obedientiam obligationi addidisse, tum officiorum nostrorum expressiori declaratione, tum præmii, & felicitatis consequendæ, velatæ sub præmiorum temporalium promissione, ampliore revelatione, tum novi exempli, & omnino ἐξαρτὶν, mortem pro nobis obeundo, propositione; magna motivorum ad charitatem & obedientiam accessione. Ex iis omnibus sequi Evangelium dici posse eatenus Lege perfectius, & majorem à Christi

page.notes: Greek words "πολιτείας" and "ἐξαρτὶν" are uncertain in the printed form ("ἐξαιρέτως" likely); marked as read. Final word "Christi" is a catchword-like fragment at the foot right, printed as "Chri-" with the hyphen; treated as text. Two-line stain at the lower left not transcribed.
